title: dna damage modulates sleep drive in basal cnidarians with divergent chronotypes
core_idea: Empirically define sleep in two basal cnidarians using behavioral criteria and investigate how light, circadian and homeostatic processes, and melatonin regulate species-specific sleep timing (chronotypes), while assessing the relationship between sleep, neuronal DNA damage, and genomic stability under stressors (sleep deprivation, UV radiation, mutagens).
tldr: Study aims to define and compare sleep regulation in two cnidarians and to examine links between sleep regulation and DNA damage/genome stability under cellular stress.
